headline: Two sessions after the buyback headline the 30y is back at 5.24% — and Walmart's 2.6% comps did the rest of Thursday's damage.
stance: Wednesday's long-end relief is more than half retraced this morning, with the first actual buyback still three weeks out on Sept 9. Walmart missing comps while raising its full-year guide gave equities the same shape of problem: the headline held, the run-rate did not.

news.head: Walmart: 2.6% comps, stock -9.15%
news.body: US comps rose 2.6% against about 3.7% expected. Adjusted EPS $0.81 beat $0.74 and the full-year guide went up; Q3 guidance $0.62-0.64 sits under $0.68.

news.head: Washington turns the screw on Iran
news.body: Brent $93.56 (~6am ET), more than 5% higher on the week and heading for a second straight weekly gain with the Hormuz standoff unresolved.

news.head: Claims 206k, no crack in the labour data
news.body: 206k for the week to Aug 15, four-week average 204k: the first labour reading since July payrolls contracted, and it did not confirm the contraction.

implications: A support operation that has not started is worth about one session of price. Duration relief now has to come from Warsh at Jackson Hole, not from Treasury's operating calendar.
The front end has not moved in four sessions. Every basis point of this week's curve move is term premium and inflation compensation - none of it a changed Fed path.

watch.head: Flash PMIs, 9:45am ET
watch.body: The only activity reading on today's calendar and the first August data point. Prices paid is the line that matters with Brent above $93.

watch.head: Whether crude closes a second weekly gain
watch.body: Brent is up more than 5% this week (~6am ET). A close here carries Hormuz headline risk into the weekend with the price at the 89th %ile of three years.

watch.head: The dollar's weekly close
watch.body: DXY 98.80 (~5am ET), about 0.9% lower on the week. Soft dollar with crude and gold both bid is the inflation-compensation trade, not a growth trade.

watch.head: Jackson Hole, Aug 27-29
watch.body: Warsh's first symposium as chair. The hike constituency in the July minutes has not been answered by any data since, and PCE lands the day before.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 30y 5.24%, 20y 5.23% (~6am ET) against a 5.187% close on Wednesday - more than half the buyback rally handed back before a single bond is bought.
None of Thursday's back-up was real yields; breakevens carried all of it. The long end is repricing Brent above $93, the one thing a buyback cannot fix.
Gold $4,538/oz, +0.5% (~6am ET), on a third straight weekly gain with real yields flat. That is a currency and volatility bid, not a rates bid.
sections.positioning: Fresh in commodities: Brent has held the 89th %ile of three years for three sessions, a new extreme. Spec net long gold at the 91st is standing background, not a new move.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Ross +7.95% after hours on a raised full-year guide, the same evening Walmart guided Q3 below consensus. Trade-down is a share shift, not a spending stop.
Futures higher: Nasdaq 100 +0.5%, S&P 500 +0.2%, Dow +128 (~5am ET). The bid is in the part of the tape Thursday's retail print did not touch.
Bitcoin above $71,000, up more than 10% in two sessions and the strongest since early June, on a White House push for the CLARITY Act.
sections.positioning: New this week: spec net long S&P 500 futures jumped 11 points to the 91st %ile with hedgers at the opposite end. That length went on before Walmart printed.

single_name.note: Bakkt - new to the screen, insider buy filed Aug 19, above its 200-day. 6.3 days to cover at a 1.31% borrow into a crypto tape at a two-month high.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Credit did not confirm Thursday's equity drop: the HY/IG cross barely moved and funding spreads stayed through OIS. One retailer's multiple, not a system.
Bank credit +6.2% y/y, syndicated loan rate 7.04%. Private borrowing costs have not followed the long end up - the term-premium move is not in the real economy yet.
sections.positioning: Dealer IG inventory has sat at the 14th %ile for three weeks - background, not a new move. It is the capacity behind any forced sale, and it has not rebuilt.

ideas.line: 3 open · 0 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
